reasoning_traces.think:
The bridge-fit operator combines leak-free prior features into a logistic regression model, producing a first directional probability. This probability is not calibrated for betting odds but serves as a pure directional signal. The spread-bucket table provides a reference scoring baseline using fixed spreads. When the bridge-fit beats the spread-bucket in Brier score, it indicates superior calibration on the same test set. However, the home-sign analysis reveals that stadium effects (dome/neutral vs. outdoor) and game momentum features (scoring/rest) carry expected signs, suggesting the model learns meaningful patterns rather than fitting noise. Cross-layer veto conditions require ensuring that prior features do not leak future information and that the directional signal remains robust under different venue and timing splits.
